chunks: And by this chain, from Hafs, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The example of the people on the Day of Resurrection when they stand before the Lord of the Worlds is like the arrow in the quiver; it has no space on the ground except for the place of its foot, like the arrow in the quiver, not able to move here or there.

key_terms.لِرَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ: Before the Lord of the Worlds

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphor used in Shia hadith to describe human movement on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) employs the metaphor of an arrow in a quiver to illustrate the absolute immobilization of the soul during the intense scrutiny of the Day of Judgment, where every individual is confined to the precise 'spot' of their accountability. This imagery underscores the Shia theological concept of *Hisab* (detailed reckoning), emphasizing that while the body remains stationary, the spiritual reality is one of intense, inescapable focus on one's deeds. The comparison highlights the helplessness of the human condition before the Divine Majesty, reinforcing the urgency of self-accounting (*Muhasabah*) in daily life.

en.hubeali: H 14558 – And by this chain, from Hafs, who has reported the following: Abu Abdullahasws said:

‘The example of the people of the Day of Judgement when they stand before the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> of the Worlds, where they will have no space for movement for themselves except for their feet, like the arrows (tightly packed) in the quiver, not having the ability for going over there or over there’.
en.sarwar: 110. And by this chain, from Hafs, who has reported the following: Abu Abdullah (a.s.) said:

‘The example of the people of the Day of Judgement when they stand before the Lord (azwj) of the Worlds, where they will have no space for movement for themselves except for their feet, like the arrows (tightly packed) in the quiver, not having the ability for going over there or over there’.
